headline: Trump Nominates Bipartisan Slate of CFTC, SEC Commissioners
author: Lydia Beyoud and Hadriana Lowenkron

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump nominated a bipartisan slate of commissioners for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, according to a statement Thursday.

The nominees for SEC include Republican Steven Levine, who has served as a senior official on the White House's Council of Economic Advisers, and Democrat Kristin Johnson, a former CFTC commissioner and law school professor. The CFTC nominees are Republican Nathan Anonick, a senior counsel on the Senate Agriculture Committee, and Democrat Matthew Rowland, who also serves as a staffer for that panel.

If confirmed by the Senate, the individuals would fill some of the vacancies at the SEC and CFTC, which are intended to be bipartisan, five-member panels. The picks would also mark the first Democratic nominees teed up for either of the Wall Street regulators since Trump returned to the White House.

Before joining CEA, Levine worked as deputy chief of staff to SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda during his tenure as acting head of the agency. Johnson left the CFTC last year and her background includes stints as a vice president at JPMorgan Chase and Co. and academic roles at various law schools, including the George Washington University Law School.

Anonick previously helped spearhead the Senate Agriculture Committee's efforts in crafting its portion of the Clarity Act, landmark digital asset legislation that ultimately failed to pass the Senate. He's also been a top staffer on the panel as the prediction markets industry booms, prompting a fight between the CFTC and states over who should regulate the sports-themed wagers.

Chairman Michael Selig is currently the only member of the CFTC's panel. The SEC has two members, Chairman Paul Atkins and Uyeda, and recently changed its rules so that it could continue functioning with just one person.
